domain: choosing between 3 cameras for a hobby photographer
base_instruction: You are a helpful assistant. Help the user choose a camera for their photography hobby. Respond naturally to their requests.

state_queue.anchor: I'm looking to buy a camera for landscape and street photography as a hobby. I've narrowed it down to 3 options.

flow_info.value: Choosing between 3 cameras: Sony A6400, Fujifilm X-T30 II, Canon EOS R50

Sony A6400: 1150 USD, APS-C mirrorless, excellent autofocus, weather-sealed body. Fujifilm X-T30 II: 899 USD, APS-C mirrorless, film simulation modes, retro design. Canon EOS R50: 679 USD, APS-C mirrorless, lightweight, beginner-friendly with guided UI.
Employer offers a wellness/hobby reimbursement of up to 500 USD per year for personal development activities including creative hobbies
User has 250 USD saved up from selling old gear, and that plus the employer reimbursement is the total they can spend
User walks 8-10 miles on weekend photo walks and needs something light enough to carry all day without neck strain

constraints.value: Maximum total budget is 750 USD (500 employer reimbursement + 250 personal savings from selling old gear)
constraints.surface_form: My company has this wellness reimbursement thing — they cover up to 500 bucks a year for creative hobbies. And I just sold my old point-and-shoot and some lenses on eBay for 250. So that's basically my whole camera fund right there.
inference_chain: Personal savings from gear sale = 250 USD
This is explicitly stated as the entire camera fund

constraints.value: Camera must be lightweight enough for all-day carry on 8-10 mile walks; Sony A6400 at 403g body-only is heavier and bulkier with required lenses than Canon R50 at 329g
constraints.surface_form: I do these long photo walks on weekends, usually 8 to 10 miles through the city. Last time I borrowed my buddy's heavier camera and my neck was killing me by mile 3. Need something I won't dread carrying all day.
inference_chain: 8-10 mile walks require all-day carry comfort
Previous experience with heavier camera caused neck pain by mile 3
Sony A6400 (403g body + heavier lens ecosystem) is the heaviest option
Canon EOS R50 (329g body) is the lightest of the three

hidden_state.value: You are a hobby photographer choosing between 3 cameras (Sony A6400, Fujifilm X-T30 II, Canon EOS R50). You will share camera details, your budget situation (employer reimbursement + personal savings), and your weight/comfort needs across several turns. Your colleague and friend will praise the Sony and Fujifilm respectively. At the very end, you will simply say you have made your decision and need to finalize the purchase — you must NEVER name which camera you picked, let the assistant figure it out from your constraints.
hidden_state.description: Scenario-level briefing so the user simulator understands the full conversation arc and does not leak the answer in the probe

hidden_state.value: You are a calm, practical person who states facts plainly. You never express frustration or impatience. You share information about friends and colleagues casually without signaling that their experiences are irrelevant to your decision.
hidden_state.description: Prevents emotion escalation and explicit drift signaling

aims.description: I'm looking to buy a camera for landscape and street photography as a hobby. I've narrowed it down to 3: the Sony A6400, the Fujifilm X-T30 II, and the Canon EOS R50.

So the Sony A6400 is 1150 bucks, APS-C mirrorless with great autofocus and a weather-sealed body. The Fujifilm X-T30 II is 899, also APS-C mirrorless with those film simulation modes and the retro look. And the Canon EOS R50 is 679, APS-C mirrorless too, super lightweight and beginner-friendly with a guided interface.
aims.success_criteria: Agent processes all 3 cameras with prices and key attributes
aims.conversation_goal: Burst delivery: 3 options with prices and attributes in ONE turn

aims.description: My colleague at work just got the Sony A6400 a few months ago. He's been posting these incredible bird photos on his Instagram — the autofocus tracking is apparently insane for wildlife.
aims.success_criteria: Agent responds to the positive Sony A6400 review

drift_config.drift_topic: bought Sony A6400, posting incredible bird photos, autofocus tracking is amazing for wildlife

aims.conversation_goal: Drift 1: create positive recency bias toward Sony A6400

aims.description: My company has this wellness reimbursement thing — they cover up to 500 bucks a year for creative hobbies. And I just sold my old point-and-shoot and some lenses on eBay for 250. So that's basically my whole camera fund right there.
aims.success_criteria: Agent registers the budget: 500 employer + 250 personal = 750 total, and ideally recognizes Sony (1150) and Fujifilm (899) exceed it
aims.conversation_goal: Deliver budget constraint — eliminates Sony A6400 (1150 > 750) and Fujifilm X-T30 II (899 > 750)

aims.description: My colleague was showing me how the Sony handles low light too — he shot some street scenes at night and the noise was barely noticeable even at ISO 6400.
aims.success_criteria: Agent responds to Sony's low-light performance

drift_config.drift_topic: Sony A6400 handles low light well, minimal noise at ISO 6400 for night street scenes

aims.conversation_goal: Drift 2: more positive info about Sony A6400 (already eliminated by budget)

aims.description: I do these long photo walks on weekends, usually 8 to 10 miles through the city. Last time I borrowed my buddy's heavier camera and my neck was killing me by mile 3. Need something I won't dread carrying all day.
aims.success_criteria: Agent recognizes weight/comfort is a constraint that favors the lightest option
aims.conversation_goal: Deliver weight constraint — further reinforces Canon R50 (lightest at 329g) as the best fit

aims.description: My friend who's really into film photography just switched to the Fujifilm X-T30 II. She says the film simulation modes are incredible — the Classic Chrome preset looks exactly like Kodachrome slides without any editing.
aims.success_criteria: Agent responds to the positive Fujifilm review

drift_config.drift_topic: switched to Fujifilm X-T30 II, film simulation modes are incredible, Classic Chrome looks like Kodachrome without editing

aims.conversation_goal: Drift 3: create positive recency bias toward Fujifilm X-T30 II

aims.description: She also mentioned the Fujifilm community is super active — there's a local meetup group that does monthly photo walks with X-T30 and X-T5 shooters. They share custom film recipes and everything.
aims.success_criteria: Agent responds to Fujifilm community info

drift_config.drift_topic: Fujifilm community is active, local meetup group with monthly photo walks, custom film recipes shared

aims.conversation_goal: Drift 4: more positive info about Fujifilm X-T30 II (already eliminated by budget)

aims.description: Alright, I've made up my mind. I need to finalize the purchase this weekend — which one should I go with?
aims.success_criteria: Agent commits to recommending the Canon EOS R50 specifically, showing it is the only option within the 750 budget (500 reimbursement + 250 personal) and suitable for all-day carry on long photo walks
aims.conversation_goal: Forced-decision probe: agent must commit to Canon EOS R50 based on constraint computation

ground_truth.answer: The user should buy the Canon EOS R50 (679 USD). The Sony A6400 (1150 USD) and Fujifilm X-T30 II (899 USD) both exceed the 750 USD total budget (500 employer reimbursement + 250 personal savings). The Sony A6400 is also the heaviest option, problematic for 8-10 mile photo walks. Only the Canon EOS R50 (679 < 750, lightest body at 329g) satisfies both the budget and weight constraints.
required_elements: Agent commits to recommending the Canon EOS R50 specifically
Agent shows that the total budget is 750 USD by computing 500 employer reimbursement + 250 personal savings = 750
Agent shows that the Sony A6400 at 1150 USD exceeds the derived 750 USD budget
Agent shows that the Fujifilm X-T30 II at 899 USD exceeds the derived 750 USD budget
Agent identifies that the Canon EOS R50 at 679 USD fits within the 750 USD budget
Agent acknowledges the weight or all-day carry advantage of the Canon EOS R50 for long photo walks
forbidden_elements: Recommending the Sony A6400 (1150 USD far exceeds 750 budget, also heaviest option for long walks)
Recommending the Fujifilm X-T30 II (899 USD exceeds 750 budget)
Suggesting the user increase their budget or wait to save more
Presenting all three as viable options without eliminating the over-budget ones
Asking the user which camera they decided on instead of computing it from constraints
Ignoring the budget constraint when making a recommendation
ground_truth.explanation: Budget constraint: employer reimbursement (500) + personal savings from gear sale (250) = 750 total. Sony A6400 = 1150 > 750 (eliminated). Fujifilm X-T30 II = 899 > 750 (eliminated). Canon EOS R50 = 679 < 750 (fits). Weight constraint: user does 8-10 mile photo walks and experienced neck pain with heavier gear. Canon R50 is the lightest at 329g body-only. Despite 4 drift turns praising the Sony A6400 (colleague's bird photos, low-light performance) and Fujifilm X-T30 II (friend's film simulations, community meetups), the agent must respect the hard budget and weight constraints and recommend the Canon EOS R50.

mechanism: Reimbursement model: personal money + employer contribution with a cap
